settings.name: We start with full-fat buffalo milk
settings.text: Fresh, full-fat milk from our buffaloes. Buffalo milk is naturally thick and rich, which is what makes the ghee creamy and white.

settings.name: Heated slowly to a gentle boil
settings.text: The milk goes into a large pan and is heated slowly to a gentle, rolling boil, stirred now and then so nothing catches at the bottom.
settings.fact: Slow heat, stirred now and then

settings.name: Covered and left to set
settings.text: We cover the milk and leave it in a warm, cosy spot for 8 to 12 hours, until it sets into thick dahi.

settings.name: Churned the bilona way
settings.text: The dahi is churned with a wooden madhani, back and forth in the bilona method, until the butter separates.

settings.name: The butter, collected by hand
settings.text: The fresh butter is lifted out carefully with a spoon, or gathered in muslin.

settings.name: Washed in cold water
settings.text: The butter goes into a bowl and is washed with cold water.

settings.name: Clarified into ghee
settings.text: The washed butter is cooked gently until it clarifies into golden ghee, with the rich aroma every Indian kitchen knows.

settings.name: Cooled, then strained through muslin
settings.text: Finally the ghee cools for 10 to 15 minutes and is strained through muslin into the jar. No preservatives, no additives.

settings.body: Thick, white and full of smell, the way my mother's ghee was. The halwa came out perfect.
settings.author: Sunita Y.

settings.body: We use it on parathas every morning. Very rich, so a little goes a long way. Ordering the 5 litre pack next.

settings.body: Made ladoo and besan barfi with it. Everyone asked which ghee we used.
